title: False Herd · Player mech
summary:
A piloted machine disguised as a juvenile herd animal. The dash and resting views explore how the same back fins can signal a change of direction and disappear into the shell. The ribbed joints could be living tissue or manufactured bellows. Both final views are open for review.

**Original lore · first pitch**

Autonomous giants migrate across the world, and settlements survive by traveling inside the herd. Your mech is a shepherd disguised as one of the juveniles. Its loose radiator fins imitate ears, and its long counterweight gives it the right gait. A run begins when a young machine strays toward a settlement. The unnerving moment comes when the herd stops walking and every head turns toward you.

**Original lore · player mech pitch**

Migrant creatures are so large that towns shelter in the furrows they leave behind. Smaller animals travel alongside them. People build mechs that can pass for members of that ecosystem, because an armed convoy draws predators and a limping juvenile draws protection. Your job is to keep one particular giant on its ancestral route. A district has been built across its old nesting ground, and the people who hired you knew that before you left.

items.title: Salt-flat dash
items.body:
A single black fin opens above the ivory back as the hip booster fires. The long neck stays low and the inside foot catches the mech’s weight. The furrows and the distant animal place its movement on the herd’s migration route.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/false-herd/quick-boost-v001.png)
items.alt: Ivory herd-mimic mech banking across a salt flat with one black dorsal fin fanned out and a giant animal on the horizon.
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a single cinematic landscape illustration of the original False Herd player mech, a piloted herd-mimic. Premium game-development keyframe, widescreen 3:2. This is an animal-shaped piece of heavy equipment seen banking into a lateral quick-boost on wind-polished salt. Back three-quarter chase camera, at hip height, slightly off its right flank so the back mechanisms are clear and the turned head shows the blunt ivory face in profile. One mech only. Entire mech and extended fin in frame, from head to both feet, occupying about three quarters of image height. Ground-level flecks of salt show its direction of travel and the tremendous weight of its planted foot. Low horizon, pale smoky sky and vast empty distance, quiet landscape with parallel migration furrows. One very faint immense moving shape in the distant haze is enough.
The mech is an unmistakably PILOTED eight-metre biped. Its design mimics a gangly juvenile wader: a short blank rounded blunted ivory brow shield with a single recessed dark sensor seam, no mouth or beak; elongated forward-set neck shrouded in parallel black folded bellows; high humped armored back sheltering a sealed pilot capsule with small bolted hatch. Two muscular long machine legs have a zigzag birdlike crouch and broad split hoof-like metal feet. Two agile mechanical arms each end in an ordinary segmented human-pattern manipulator, dark square fingers, broad wrist cuff, opposing thumb. Arms held apart from the torso with meaningful negative space. One back panel has a small muted oxblood identification stripe. Broad worn ivory-ceramic armor on upper shoulders and parts of limbs, charcoal load-bearing frame, salt deposits at plate edges. Heavy broad masses with quiet smooth surfaces, careful selective detail in moving joints. No exposed flesh, the living or manufactured origin of the folds remains ambiguous.
Signature silhouette: precisely two black collapsible radiator fins on the upper back. Right dorsal fin has fanned open to catch this turn, a short broad asymmetrical folding sail with four structural battens and rippled matte charcoal membrane, sharply silhouetted against the white sky; left dorsal fin is tightly furled against the spine, distinct from the deployed one. Fins are shorter than an arm. A low compact hip booster kicks up a short plume of salt. No giant angel or bat wings, arms do not function as wings. Keep the silhouette legible at thumbnail size, shadow detail visible, crisp helmet, fins, limbs. Sophisticated painterly industrial sci-fi concept art, textured graphite underdrawing and dry-brushed pigments, cool gray morning light, pale warm salt, bruised gray sky, sparse rust accents. Original composition, believable mass and animal balance. No type, logos, borders, HUD, panels, swords, guns, extra limbs or humans.

items.title: At rest
items.body:
The folded fin battens follow the slope of the back. A blank sensor mask, ribbed neck and split feet give the machine its wary posture. The shoulder stripe, bolted hatch and paired wrist cuffs identify it as a piloted frame. Both arms and hands are clear in this revised front study.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/false-herd/front-v002.png)
items.alt: Front view of a salt-worn ivory mech with a burgundy shoulder stripe, tucked black fins, two articulated hands and split hooves.
items.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Repair the arm anatomy in this portrait of the False Herd mech. It presently shows THREE arms: one at the outer left edge, one through the center overlapping the near ivory thigh, and one at the outer right edge. Deliver a clean, truly front-facing inspection view that unambiguously shows exactly TWO arms, ONE left and ONE right, attached at one shoulder per side. There must be an empty gap between each arm and the torso from elbows to wrists; remove the central forearm and central hand entirely. Orient the torso toward the camera enough that both shoulders can be seen clearly flanking the upper chest. Each of the two wrists has one open dark segmented hand hanging outboard of the thighs, clearly silhouetted against the neutral backdrop. Let the head cant slightly to one side so the ribbed black neck peeks through. Preserve this specific animal-mimic cockpit shell, blank ivory face with single narrow sensor slit, broad sloped ivory armor and one faded burgundy stripe, black furled radiator fins, long crouched pair of mechanical legs, broad two-toed feet, intact human-scale service hatch, salt-worn finish and painterly industrial realism. Chest and pelvis on the centerline; clear unobstructed view of both thighs and knees. Single full-body mech in a portrait image, quiet warm grey studio, safe margins for feet and head, no words or props.

items.body:

items.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Create a companion front three-quarter character study of the SAME False Herd player mech in the provided image. Use that image as the authoritative source for proportions, shapes, finishes, hardware and silhouette. One standalone full-body portrait 2:3, a single machine, plain warm ash-gray studio cyclorama and grounded soft contact shadow. Full head, hands and feet visible with generous margins. Clean, exacting hand-painted industrial design plate. The viewer is seeing this machine from ahead, offset about 25 degrees, at the height of its sternum, long lens. BOTH back fins are now neatly FURLED flat and parallel against the armored back, unspread. Pose is still, the weight poised on two feet, one leg half a step ahead; neck reaching out low like a wary young herd animal, the sensor seam pointed slightly past the viewer. In this view you can see the blunt smooth ivory mask with its dark horizontal sensor seam, broad shoulder shells sloping over a sealed pilot chest, and black accordion neck nested into the torso. Preserve the long neck and sloping hump, matte salt-abraded ivory armor, charcoal mechanisms, muted burgundy shoulder stripe, long folded wader-like legs with broad split mechanical hooves, matching ordinary human-pattern mechanical grippers with a broad wrist, rectangular articulated digits and opposing thumb. Hands empty and visible, elbows held slightly away from the body. Carry forward the mass and particular character of the reference. The biological hint comes from the posture and soft ribbed joint covers, alongside believable armor seams and hinges. Broad flat daylight, crisp shadow under each overlap, subtle pencil and gouache surface, ample light to read the dark shapes in the belly. No other figures, drawings, insert, environment detail, technical callouts, text, captions, insignia, logos, weapons or HUD. This should feel like a candid portrait of a wary machine on the service floor, not a human standing at attention.
